AUTHOR: Böer
TITLE: Segmentation of Fish in Realistic Underwater Scenes using Lightweight Deep Learning Models
VENUE: Proceedings of ROBOVIS 2021 (2nd International Conference on Robotics, Computer Vision and Intelligent Systems)
REGION: North Sea (45 nm west of Sylt, 22 m depth) and Kiel Fjord (Baltic Sea), Germany
DATA: Own footage from a stationary seafloor stereo sensor platform (Photonis Nocturn XL low-light monochrome cameras); 600 labeled images + 1148-image separate test set
V_EV: [V1 recoded NR on verification: statement not about the study's own water clarity] Sec. 3.1: 'deployed at seafloor level, at a depth of 22m'; Sec. 4.3: 'This explains the poor visibility in the lower part of the image' (no stratified results)
D2: 600 images random 80/10/10 plus a separate 1,148-image test set from a different day (headline results)
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'very similar samples may appear in the test and training set... a separate test set of 1148 images, that where recorded on a different day'
R_EV: Sec. 4.3: 'The performance of each model on the independent test set of 1148 images'; same platform, cameras and deployment
C_EV: Sec. 4.2: 'All segmentation results were thresholded at a confidence value of 0.5 to obtain binary masks.' (default threshold, no justification or false-positive check)
E_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'The metrics used for the validation of the models are the pixel-level accuracy and Intersection-over-Union (IoU)' (biomass/length only as future work)
ARCH: Pruned PSPNet and DeepLabv3 with MobileNetV2 encoder (first 3 stages), Dice loss, PyTorch
METR: Pixel accuracy (96.8% PSPNet), IoU (73.8%), inference FPS, model size
NOTE: D1 coded as 조사일 because the reported results (Table 1) are on a 1148-image test set recorded on a different day, explicitly motivated by near-duplicate leakage concern (D4 = Y); the initial 600-image train/val/test split itself was random at image level - verifier may prefer D1 = 이미지/프레임 무작위 with D4 = Y (D_ALL = P). R1 = N because the different-day test set uses the same platform, cameras and sites (not external by the review definition), although the paper calls it 'completely unseen data'. V2 = Y (22 m depth), V3 = Y (passive lighting, twilight described qualitatively). ENV: temperate seafloor (North Sea / Baltic), coded as nearest temperate category. NIMG = 600 + 1148. FPS 'up to 20 frames/second'. | C_ALL NA→P (classification study reporting a score threshold/reject rule; amended rule).
